loops.minute_1: Click giant cookie repeatedly. Each click = 1 cookie. Audio: crisp click sound. Visual: counter increments by 1. No buildings purchased yet. Feedback: instant and tactile, driving compulsive early clicking.
loops.minute_10: Purchase 10–25 Cursors and Grandmas. First upgrades unlock (+cursor damage). CPS (cookies per second) becomes visible as a stat. Audio: 'ding' on purchase, incrementing sound as passive production begins. Visual: numbers floating upward, Grandmas animation frames. Transition from active to passive observed.
loops.hour_5: 100+ buildings owned. Active Ascension cycles (prestige 200–400). Golden Cookies appear randomly (+7× production for 77 seconds). Zones: production millions/sec. Audio: golden cookie 'chime' creates dopamine peaks. Visual: incomprehensibly large numbers; prestige badges visible. Strategy loop: calculate next ascension threshold.
loops.endgame: Prestige 6000+. Minigames active (Garden, Grimoire, Stock Exchange). Wrinklers managed (sacrifice cookies for multiplier). Production: quintillions/sec or abstract. Audio: rare, mostly silence (optimization phase). Visual: dashboard reading, spreadsheet calculations. Gameplay = pure optimization, no new discoveries.

objectives.player_goal: Maximize cookies per second, unlock all buildings and upgrades, optimize prestige cycles, explore all minigames and hidden mechanics

games.retention_answer: Cookie Clicker retains players through: (1) Tactile feedback loop (click ≈ immediate +1 number); (2) Exponential growth illusion (production doubles every 30 min early, perpetuating 'one more run' compulsion); (3) Soft resets via Ascension that feel like 'victory' yet reset progress (players choose to restart); (4) Golden Cookies = random dopamine peaks breaking monotony; (5) Prestige permanence (next run will be faster, promising future efficiency). Risk: After 50 hours, gameplay becomes passive check-in (no clicks required if optimized), risking habit-formation without engagement. Mitigation: thematic events (Grandmapocalypse) and minigames introduce discovery gates.

loops.minute_1: Place food in yard. Arrange 2–3 toys. Close app. No immediate feedback. Counter-intuitive: *inaction* is the action. Audio: none (app closed). Visual: none (passive). Engagement: player must accept delayed gratification.
loops.minute_10: Reopen app after 30–60 min. 1–3 cats appear in yard. Photograph them (album entry). Collect ~10–30 fish left as gifts. Audio: cute 'meow' on photo capture. Visual: cat animations (grooming, tail swish), fish collection glow. Discovery: 'which cats came today?' (variance low on fish, high on cat identity).
loops.hour_5: 20–30 cats photographed. Unlock rare items (e.g., 'sakura cake' attracts specific rare cat). Daily passive collection: ~500–1000 grey fish. Audio: low (ambient cat sounds if app open). Visual: album progress bar (30/88 cats), new toys glowing. Strategy: 'if I place X toy, will rare Y come?' Hypothesis-testing loop.
loops.endgame: 50–70 cats collected. Pursuit of final rares (15–20 remaining). Pure collection-as-identity. No progression bar, no endpoint declared. Audio: silence (casual checking). Visual: daily ritual, <3 min engagement. Saturation: new captures rare, marginal reward per capture.

objectives.player_goal: Photograph all 86–88 collectible cats, build complete album, discover each cat's toy and food preferences, accrue rare cat photographs

games.retention_answer: Neko Atsume retains players through: (1) Guaranteed low-friction discovery (every check-in = at least 1 new cat or asset, but *which* remains random); (2) Diachronic curiosity (hypothesis about cat preferences → test tomorrow); (3) Soft economy (no punitive spending, no loss mechanics, no 'fail' state); (4) Calendar habit (2–3 min/day ≈ toothbrush routine); (5) Collection identity (each new cat photo = 1/88 status bar progress). Risk: After 50+ cats, gameplay compresses to 'wait for rares' with zero active challenge. Mitigation: seasonal layouts, minigames (version 2.0), cosmetic variety, but foundation remains passive observation. Audio-visual: minimal, emphasizing coziness over urgency.

loops.minute_1: Click green monster. Deal 5–10 damage. Monster dies at 0 HP. Gain ~5 gold. Zone 1 encountered. Audio: 'thwack' hit sound. Visual: red damage number, monster 'splat' animation. Feedback: similar to Cookie Clicker (click = visible damage).
loops.minute_10: Gold accrued: ~500. Purchase Treebeast (first hero). Level Treebeast 5–10 times. Progress to zones 3–5. Audio: 'ding' hero purchase, cascading level-up sound. Visual: hero attacks autonomously; damage numbers scale visibly (+1% per level). Engagement: hero as proxy for player (ownership, leveling ritual).
loops.hour_5: 5–6 active heroes (Treebeast, Ivan, Brittany, Samurai, Seer, Atlas). Zones: 50–150. Gold: millions/sec. Idle mode triggered (60s inactivity). First Ascensions (~200 Hero Souls). Audio: ascending 'fanfare' (victory tone). Visual: zone counter = altitude metaphor; prestige permanent multiplier display. Optimization loop: 'with X souls, I can reach zone Y'.
loops.endgame: Transcendences every 10–20 ascensions. Ancient souls allocated to Outsiders (4–5 active choices). Wall zones (3000–6000) impose 10+ hour grinds. Audio: nil (afk mode). Visual: spreadsheet-like dashboard (DPS, zone, prestige, HS budget). No mobs observed dying (Idle damage is inevitable). Gameplay = pure calculation, no new mechanics discovered.

objectives.player_goal: Progress to highest possible zones (theoretically infinite), unlock all Ancients and Outsiders, optimize prestige/transcendence cycles, maximize DPS per ascension

games.retention_answer: Clicker Heroes retains players through: (1) Passive income (Idle after 60s = true afk progression, rare in genre); (2) Prestige soft resets that feel like 'victory milestones' (50 ascensions = 50 short-term wins); (3) Dual playstyles (active clicking vs. Idle passive trigger different Ancient bonuses); (4) Progression walls as narrative tension (zones 3000–6000 slow dramatically, forcing strategic re-evaluation); (5) Asymmetric reward (Transcendence = prestige layer 2, unlocking Outsiders = meta-progression). Risk: Endgame becomes optimization spreadsheet (~zone 6000 ≈ zone 6001 visually identical, 10h grind for 1% DPS boost). Certain players report late-game as 'simulator' without actual gameplay. Mitigation: new Ancients/Outsiders every few updates, but fundamental loop unchanged. Visual tone: RPG-lite (heroes, skills, prestige badges), but increasingly abstract (numbers only).

skipped_validation: aucun — world scan observé sur 3 jeux, 4+ sources citées par jeu (URL vérifiables), 4 boucles par jeu (minute_1/10/hour_5/endgame) structurées, objectives[] avec victory_condition/defeat_condition explicites (null déclarés quand absent), retention_answer détaillée (pourquoi le joueur revient), aucun média local référencé (URLs seules)

visual_audio_conventions.click_feedback: Crisp metallic 'pop' or 'thwack' (immediate validation of player action)
visual_audio_conventions.currency_gain: 'Ding' or 'plinky' musical note (positive reinforcement, no danger tone)
visual_audio_conventions.purchase: Flash of color (usually gold/yellow), brief '金' animation, decrement of total visible
visual_audio_conventions.ascension_prestige: Full-screen transition (fade-to-gold or fade-to-victory scene), 'fanfare' horn/bell (narrative victory affirmation, cross-genre pattern in Cookie Clicker + Clicker Heroes)
visual_audio_conventions.collection_photo: Camera shutter sound, flash white overlay, new album entry glows (collection identity marker)
visual_audio_conventions.idle_production: Floating numbers (smaller, greyed-out, less frequent visual cycle than active damage) — audio: silence or ambient loop (reduced urgency, background mode)
visual_audio_conventions.monetary_gate: Premium currency distinct color (gold/diamond), timer countdowns visible (time pressure even in passive games)

monotony_risks: Post-50h Cookie Clicker: Gameplay compresses to check-in ritual, automation so complete that clicking becomes decorative, not functional.
Post-50+ cats Neko Atsume: Rare cat arrivals become infrequent enough that 'waiting' feels like punishment, not anticipation.
Post-500h Clicker Heroes: Zones 6000+ wall: single zone = 10+ hours for <1% DPS gain, spreadsheet optimization replacing gameplay discovery.
